what_it_does: The PNT layer produces, protects, fuses and distributes four-dimensional state (x, y, z, and time) for every platform, weapon, radio and C2 node. It underpins the rest of C4ISR: sensor georegistration, track correlation, fires targeting, network time for Link 16/SATCOM/crypto, and the common operating picture all consume PNT. Technically it comprises (1) space and terrestrial signal sources (GPS incl. encrypted M-code, LEO-PNT, eLoran/VLF, signals of opportunity), (2) onboard relative sensors (IMUs, clocks, odometry, vision, magnetometers, celestial, quantum sensors), (3) a fusion engine that estimates position/velocity/attitude/time and, increasingly, an assurance/integrity verdict per source (Army PNT Reference Architecture v1.0, 2018), (4) NAVWAR defensive functions (anti-jam antennas, interference detection, spoof rejection) and (5) time transfer across networks so that platforms can exchange USNO-traceable time without GPS. Policy requires every platform with a validated PNT requirement to have a DoD-approved primary source (GPS PPS) plus at least one GPS-independent alternate (OPNAVINST 9420.1C para 5.a(3); DoDI 4650.08 NAVWAR compliance).

current_architecture.description: GPS remains the core: DoD's 2020 PNT S&T Roadmap and GAO-21-320SP state GPS will stay the primary source with alternative sources complementing it and cross-checking each other. Platforms carry a GPS receiver (SAASM today, M-code via MGUE cards as they arrive), an inertial unit and a clock; the Army's MAPS/DAPS and the Navy's GPNTS add a fusion engine that ingests multiple sources and outputs a single assured PVT plus assurance. The Army leads a DoD-wide MOSA: service PNT reference architectures (Army v1.0 July 2018; Navy; Air Force nascent in 2021), the DARPA-originated All-Source Positioning and Navigation (ASPN) interface standard, and the government-owned pntOS fusion engine with vendor plug-ins. In 2026 the ASPN 2023 YAML data model and the pntOS C API became publicly downloadable on GitHub (Open-PNT org), with a separate government-only ASPN message set behind a citizenship/contractor gate (aspn.us). Time is distributed by GPS, holdover clocks and network time transfer over Link 16/TTNT/PTW/CDL; a Navy-led initiative seeks to make every comms system able to pass USNO-traceable time. NAVWAR compliance is a milestone gate for any system producing or using PNT (DoDI 4650.08 Section 3).

current_architecture.security_domain: Mixed. GPS PPS/M-code keys and crypto are classified/COMSEC (crypto network assignments handled by NSA and Space Force per DoDI 4650.08); NAVWAR threat assessments and PNT Oversight Council reports are classified (GAO-21-320SP fn 36). The government ASPN message set is access-controlled (citizenship + contractor verification). The Navy operator-awareness topic is explicitly CUI-only with 'no plan for work at higher classification' and no facility clearance expected for Phase II (NP004 Q&A 2026-08-28 and 2026-09-01). Civil PNT-integrity work (DHS/NIST) is fully public.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: The layer is designed to work with NO connectivity: onboard relative sensors carry the solution through outages. However absolute corrections (GPS, LEO-PNT, SoOP, celestial/magnetic map updates 'days to months', corrections) and fleet-wide interference awareness depend on RF or network reach. The Navy requires the awareness capability including all analytics and AI inference to run 100% air-gapped aboard individual ships with no reliance on shore or cloud (NP004 Q&A 2026-08-20).
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Without GPS/absolute sources, inertial and clock errors grow unbounded (GAO fig. 6): CSACs are about 100x worse than GPS after a day; ships tolerate 500 m-class fixes but munitions and fires need frequent absolute updates. Network time drifts, which eventually breaks crypto synchronization and Link 16 net entry (INFERENCE from GAO 3.3.1). Operators today must reconcile several fragmented displays manually to decide whether to switch sources or drop to INS-only (NP004 Q&A). Alternative PNT technologies that rely on communications links may themselves be unavailable in a degraded environment (GAO 4.1.7).

technical_difficulty.summary: Split sharply by sub-layer. Signal sources and quantum/photonic sensors are deep-physics, manufacturing-limited problems (GAO: thermal-beam atomic sensors need 'many high-precision components and specialized assembly'; new clock architectures blocked by light-source and vacuum-chamber manufacturing). Map-matching navigation is mostly software plus data (magnetic maps, imagery) with platform-noise calibration. The fusion/assurance/awareness sub-layers are classic estimation, integrity monitoring (RAIM-like consistency, multi-source consensus, ICD-compliance checks as in the DHS PNT Integrity Library) and HMI/decision-support engineering, now buildable against public ASPN/pntOS schemas with synthetic data. The Navy explicitly wants no new sensors or algorithms for NP004, only software architecture, data integration, UX/HMI, analytics and decision support.
required_expertise: Kalman/particle-filter state estimation and INS error modeling
GNSS observables, RAIM and spoof/jam detection methods (Psiaki & Humphreys class literature; TEXBAT datasets)
ASPN/pntOS message modeling and plugin development (C API, meson)
Human-centered design for watchstanders; ECDIS/S-52 symbology and IMO bridge-alert conventions
Containerized air-gapped deployment (Iron Bank/Platform One, Kubernetes) and CMMC Level 2 practices
Explainable decision support and auditable event logging
For hardware paths: atomic physics, photonics, RF front-end and antenna design, magnetometry, precision manufacturing
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Deriving a trustworthy composite confidence across 3-8 heterogeneous sources when 'untrustworthy does not always mean the current solution is incorrect' (DHS CF) and when the adversary can also corrupt the maps/models alt-PNT relies on (GAO 4.1.7); doing this with sub-second latency, offline, and with rationale the operator trusts. Army officials told GAO that assurance determination 'is an active research area' with source-level and consensus approaches both immature (GAO-21-320SP 3.3.2).
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Open-source GNSS-SDR software receiver (GPL-3), gnss-lib-py (Stanford NavLab, PyPI 1.1.0), DHS PNT Integrity Library (BSD-3), MagNav.jl and USAF open flight data, ASPN 2023 YAML schemas, pntOS-C API, MapLibre/PMTiles for offline charts, IHO S-57 test cells, NIST/USNO holdover references, commercial MEMS IMUs, CSACs (about $2,000 each per GAO 2021), Iron Bank base images.

capital_intensity.proof_of_concept_usd: Software (assurance/awareness/tooling): $50k-$150k for a synthetic-ASPN simulator, fusion/consistency checks and an ECDIS-like HMI demo. Hardware/quantum sensor: $3M-$15M lab and team.
capital_intensity.credible_military_demo_usd: Software: $0.3M-$2M, i.e., one Navy SBIR Phase I ($315k max) plus Phase II ($2M max) including a PNTAX or fleet demonstration with GPNTS ICDs. Hardware/quantum: $15M-$60M including flight/sea trials and ruggedization.
capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: Software: $2M-$8M for GPNTS/pntOS integration, Iron Bank hardening, ATO/certification, fleet training and sustainment. Hardware: $50M-$200M+ for qualified production, consistent with Infleqtion's public-market scale and SandboxAQ's funding (RECALL).
capital_intensity.assumptions: Two founders, $250k, U.S.-based; Phase I performable entirely on synthetic ASPN/pntOS data (NP004 Q&A); no facility clearance for Phase II; integration costs dominated by government-furnished ICDs and certification rather than hardware. Hardware ranges are order-of-magnitude judgments (HYPOTHESIS) informed by GAO manufacturing findings and public funding sizes.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - for the fusion/assurance/awareness sub-layers: 'In Phase 1, vendors may use synthetic data that adheres to open-source standards (ASPN/pntOS)' (NP004 Q&A 2026-08-28); public GPS ICDs, DHS/NIST frameworks, USCG/MARAD interference advisories and open flight data (MagNav) are all unclassified. No for M-code/PPS receiver work (COMSEC keys) and for real NAVWAR threat data.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Post-award only: GPNTS ICDs and message types, the government ASPN message set (citizenship + contractor verification at aspn.us), representative Navy data sets in Phase II, and JNWC standardized threat conditions. Real jamming/spoofing signatures come from PNTAX/JNWC or civil sources (TEXBAT, Jammertest).
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Military GNSS receivers with anti-jam/PPS/M-code and associated technical data are USML-controlled (Category XII(d) class, RECALL) and M-code cryptography is COMSEC; MAPS/DAPS-type hardware is ITAR. The NP004 topic carries no ITAR banner (Q&A 2026-08-28 contrasts it with NP003) and is CUI/CMMC L2. Inertial and quantum sensor designs may be USML or EAR 7A/7E controlled. DoDI 4650.08 1.2.f restricts foreign transfer of equipment relying on civil/commercial/foreign PNT sources. Specialist export-control classification is required before a non-U.S.-person founder touches receiver or sensor technical data.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes. 'All NP004 Phase I data and activity is controlled unclassified information' (Q&A 2026-08-28); CMMC Level 2 (Self) at award; DFARS 7012 handling.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: For operator awareness on Navy ships: the government says no plan for higher classification and no facility clearance expected in Phase II (Q&A 2026-09-01). For anything touching M-code keys, NAVWAR threat assessments (classified per GAO), Link 16 time transfer or JNWC biennial assessments, yes.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not for the awareness/fusion-tooling MVP (per Navy Q&A). Required for M-code receiver, crypto, or threat-library work.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: Three distinct constraints need counsel: (1) SBIR/STTR eligibility requires a small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (SBA policy directive; the German founder's pending permanent residency and the Indonesian founder's status both matter); (2) CUI/CMMC and the aspn.us government message set gate on citizenship/contractor verification, so a non-U.S.-person co-founder may be excluded from the government-only schema and from Phase II data even though the work is unclassified; (3) ITAR technical-data access for any receiver/sensor path is a deemed-export issue. None of this is a definitive legal judgment; it is the checklist for an export-control and government-contracts attorney.

why_not_solved.explanation: No central alt-PNT program office; each service and each platform sets its own PNT requirements, so vendors face 'a range of requirements' and a market too small for economies of scale (GAO-21-320SP 4.1.1, 4.1.3, 4.1.4). The awareness layer sat between navigation, EW and C2 owners with nobody responsible.

Fielded receivers are closed systems delivered by one prime; 'because of this proprietary nature, there are few opportunities to integrate alternative PNT technologies' (GAO 4.1.6). Until ASPN/pntOS became public in 2026 there was no open surface for third-party software.

The pntOS C API (April 2026) and ASPN 2023 public release (January 2026) plus the Navy's decision to accept synthetic ASPN/pntOS data for Phase I make a software-only entry possible for the first time; quantum sensors and LEO-PNT are still manufacturing- and constellation-limited.

DoD funded the integration/MOSA fix at $17M over five years against $783M of PNT S&T; experts warned it would 'peter out' without sustained funding, and hardware vendors have little incentive to open interfaces.

NAVWAR compliance must be determined at every milestone and fleet PNT systems certified as-designed and as-installed; GAO found OT&E policy for MOSA-type systems 'a challenge' and no PNT-specific MOSA certification path, which slows any modular newcomer.

Threat conditions, PNT Oversight Council reports and PPS crypto are classified, so integrity algorithms are often tuned inside cleared prime environments rather than in open competition; civil (DHS) work stays separate.

Composite multi-source assurance is still 'an active research area' (GAO 3.3.2) and DHS CF Level 3-4 behaviors (bounded degradation, automatic recovery without disrupting output) are aspirational for most fielded equipment.

attractiveness.bull: For a two-person software team the 2026 opening is unusually clean: a named Navy transition owner (GPNTS) has published a software-only open topic with CUI-only work, no clearance expected through Phase II, synthetic ASPN/pntOS data allowed, multiple Phase I awards planned, $315k Phase I and $2M Phase II Prototype OTs, and a stated preference for commercially derived data-integration/decision-support platforms. The same assurance and awareness engine has civil analogs (DHS conformance levels, critical-infrastructure timing, maritime GNSS interference advisories) that reduce single-customer risk. Public ASPN/pntOS schemas plus open-source integrity libraries (DHS PNT Integrity, GNSS-SDR, MagNav data) mean the MVP needs no ITAR hardware. Persistent GAO findings since 2017 and daily GPS-denied testing show demand will not evaporate.
attractiveness.bear: The NP004 topic will draw many bidders (NAVWAR states multiple awards) including incumbents around GPNTS and firms with ECDIS/HMI pedigrees; SBIR ownership rules and CUI/citizenship gates cut against a team with a non-U.S.-person founder; PNT is 'nobody's business' inside DoD, so a Phase III could stall in proto-purgatory as alt-PNT S&T has for years; the deep-value hardware layers (M-code, quantum sensors, LEO-PNT, timing) are capital-intensive and prime-dominated and out of reach for $250k; and the awareness layer could be absorbed into GPNTS or a future NGC2-style C2 data layer as a feature rather than a product.
attractiveness.verdict: Attractive only in the software sub-layers (multi-source assurance/awareness, pntOS/ASPN tooling and NAVWAR test harnesses); MEDIUM-HIGH for those, LOW for sensors, signals and timing hardware. The Navy NP004 topic is the single best-documented near-term entry vehicle in this segment, but the founders' eligibility must be cleared first.

proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for novel-sensor startups (institutional pattern of demos without transition, plus classified/PoR-owned integration). Opportunity for software that lowers the integration/certification cost that causes the purgatory (pntOS plugins, synthetic-data test harnesses, assurance dashboards), provided the team ties itself to a PoR early.

candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Navigation operators must mentally fuse several fragmented displays of GPS/INS/alternate-source health to decide whether they are jammed, spoofed or broken and which fallback to take, with no composite confidence, no recommendation and no audit trail.
candidate_gaps.user: Navy ETV/ETSW and navigation team on surface combatants (initial); analogous roles on Army MAPS-equipped vehicles, aircraft and coalition ships later.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1. ETV mans the station during contested transits. 2. Watches separate GPS, INS, GPNTS and alternate-source indicators plus ECDIS. 3. Notices divergence or alarms. 4. Manually infers cause (fault vs jam vs spoof) from raw indicators and experience. 5. Consults TTPs/checklists and OOD. 6. Selects alternate source or INS-only. 7. Records actions in navigation workbook; reports interference to NAVCEN/EW cell by voice or message.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Individual system HMIs (GPNTS, INS, receiver front panels), ECDIS, paper/PDF procedures, celestial/radar/DR fixes as backup; no unified confidence or decision aid (Navy states this in the topic).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Slow, error-prone triage under workload; wrong fallback selection; no explainable rationale or replay; interference information not automatically passed to electronic support as OPNAVINST 9420.1C 5.a(11) intends.

evidence.claim: Navy states operators face fragmented interfaces that increase cognitive workload and slow decisions and seeks a 'single pane of glass' decision-support environment.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Baseline workflow is 'monitoring multiple fragmented physical displays'; the solution must both visualize source-level confidence and derive a composite confidence; must run air-gapped; 3-8 sources at 1-10 Hz; sub-second latency; explainable and auditable.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Policy already requires new PNT systems to indicate degradation to the operator and pass interference data to electronic support, with waivers for non-compliance.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Assurance determination across sources is 'an active research area' with source-level and consensus approaches; the fusion engine is responsible for evaluating assurance in the Army reference architecture.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DHS CF v2.0 defines expected Respond/Recover behaviors (Level 2: continue output while responding to a compromised source; automatic recovery without disrupting output) that equipment must expose, giving a standards basis for an awareness layer.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Until 2026 the data was locked inside proprietary receivers and program-specific ICDs; NAVWAR only now published a software-only topic and accepted synthetic ASPN/pntOS data; the buyer sat between navigation, EW and C2 owners.

candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: MEDIUM-HIGH: the GPNTS prime or IS4S could add an awareness screen; ECDIS-N vendors could extend the chart display; Navy could keep it government-developed. Mitigation: be the composite-assurance analytics and replay engine, not just a dashboard, and hold the synthetic-scenario library.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A source-agnostic 'PNT integrity graph' that ingests ASPN measurement and integrity fields from 3-8 sources, runs consistency/ICD-compliance/consensus checks (DHS PNT Integrity-style plus INS-GNSS divergence and clock-drift models), emits a composite confidence with attributed evidence, and renders on an S-52-conformant chart layer with bridge-alert-management style alerts; deterministic, explainable, replayable, containerized.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Synthetic strait-transit scenario generator (GNSS jam/spoof, INS drift, clock holdover) emitting ASPN 2023 messages; integrity engine; ECDIS-like web HMI with alert banner, source cards, composite confidence gauge, recommended fallback with rationale, event timeline/replay; Docker/Kubernetes deployment offline; user study with former ETVs measuring speed-to-decision and fallback accuracy (Navy's stated metrics).
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Phase I: synthetic ASPN/pntOS streams, public GPS ICDs, TEXBAT/Jammertest-type spoof/jam signatures, NOAA ENC cells. Phase II: GPNTS ICDs and representative Navy data sets (government-furnished post-award).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: ASPN/pntOS ingest; GPNTS message types (Phase II); optional NMEA/IEC 61162 bridge bus; Iron Bank container images; Navy ECDIS-N symbology conventions; eventual interface to EW reporting (NAVCEN, electronic support).
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Navy SBIR 26.5 topic DON26BX05-NP004 (closed 2026-09-23; expect re-issue or Phase II path), then Navy STP and Phase III via GPNTS; Army analog via PM PNT/xTech or C5ISR Center pntOS plug-in community; civil analog via DHS/CISA and maritime operators.
candidate_gaps.why_now: First-ever dedicated solicitation (Aug 2026), public ASPN/pntOS (2026), ASPN moving to an industry consortium (Jul 2026), GPS-denied testing and real-world interference at record levels, and explicit government acceptance of commercially derived platforms.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Founder eligibility (SBIR >50% U.S.-person ownership; CUI/citizenship gates on the government ASPN message set) and single-customer dependence on GPNTS; also a crowded Phase I field with multiple awards diluting the win.

candidate_gaps.title: Formation- and theater-level PNT interference and integrity picture (crowd-sourced NAVWAR situational awareness feeding the C2/EW COP)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Individual MAPS/DAPS/GPNTS units detect jamming or spoofing locally, but there is no unified, near-real-time aggregation of those reports across a formation into the EW/C2 common operating picture, so commanders cannot see where PNT is being denied or trust which tracks are position-corrupted.
candidate_gaps.user: EW/spectrum planners and battle captains at battalion through theater; JNWC and Space Force NAVWAR cells; coalition navigation warfare officers.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1. Platform receiver flags interference. 2. Crew reports by voice/chat or not at all. 3. EW cell manually plots reports; JNWC compiles assessments after the fact. 4. Civil channels (NAVCEN, MARAD, ADS-B community maps) run in parallel. 5. Commander infers denial areas from anecdotes.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: JNWC operational field assessments and biennial assessments (DoDI 4650.08); EW planning tools; RF-geolocation constellations (RECALL: HawkEye 360); civil GPS jamming maps from ADS-B; MARAD/NAVCEN advisories.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Latency (hours to days), manual re-entry, releasability barriers between platforms/coalition, and no link between interference geometry and the trustworthiness of tracks in the COP.

candidate_gaps.title: pntOS/ASPN developer tooling: synthetic-scenario generators, plug-in conformance testing and NAVWAR-compliance evidence harness for alternative PNT vendors and programs
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Every alt-PNT vendor and every PNT-using program must now prove ASPN/pntOS conformance and NAVWAR compliance, but the government's planned compliance toolkit, M&S fidelity and field-test capacity are thin, so integration remains bespoke, slow and expensive.
candidate_gaps.user: Alt-PNT sensor vendors (DIU TQS cohort, LEO-PNT, MagNav, vision-nav), platform integrators, PM PNT/NAVWAR test engineers, NAVWAR-compliance reviewers.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1. Vendor obtains ASPN/pntOS docs (public C API; government messages after vetting). 2. Writes plug-in with ad hoc test data. 3. Waits for PNTAX or a program lab slot. 4. Program runs M&S with low-fidelity alt-PNT models. 5. MDA demands NAVWAR compliance evidence at milestone; evidence assembled manually.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Spirent/Safran Skydel RF simulators (hardware-in-the-loop, costly), Army MDQDA and GIANT/CIGNM (government-internal), annual PNTAX, vendor-specific test rigs.

candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-core scenario generator + conformance test suite for pntOS plug-ins with a hosted evidence report; first users are alt-PNT vendors preparing for PNTAX; dual use for the S11-G1 HMI testing.

candidate_gaps.title: Non-GPS time distribution and holdover assurance for tactical networks and C2 nodes
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: When GPS is denied, radios, crypto and C2 servers lose their common time reference within hours to a day (CSAC holdover is about 100x worse than GPS after one day), and the Navy-led initiative to distribute USNO-traceable time over every comms link remains an S&T effort.
candidate_gaps.user: Network/timing engineers, Link 16 net managers, SATCOM/crypto custodians, data-center operators at battalion through theater.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1. GPS disciplines a master clock. 2. On loss, rubidium/cesium holdover; NTP/PTP over the LAN. 3. Link 16/TTNT/PTW carry time within their nets. 4. Operators manually monitor drift and re-sync when GPS returns.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Safran/Microchip timing servers and clocks, Iridium STL for indoor/timing, two-way satellite time transfer, network-specific time transfer; no unified cross-network timing assurance.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Specialized time-transfer modems per network; no common monitoring of holdover state across radios and servers; policy requires USNO traceability certification.

evidence.claim: DoD S&T initiative (Navy lead) aims to enable all communications systems to distribute USNO-traceable time platform-to-platform to minimize specialized time transfer modems; time-transfer techniques exist per network (CDL, CEC, Link 16, LORAN, PTW, TTNT).
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: CSAC precision about 100x worse than GPS after one day; optical clocks could give GPS-level time for a day but need 10-20x the power; new clock architectures blocked by manufacturing.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Navy policy lists alternate precise-time sources (rubidium/cesium clocks, NTP, HF voice, two-way and one-way satellite time transfer) and requires USNO-certified clocks with documented traceability.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DHS CF gives a timing resilience example (Level 3, 1.8 microsecond threshold, 80 s recovery) showing measurable timing-assurance behaviors are expected of equipment.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Iridium (public) has built a PNT/timing line via Satelles; NextNav and others pursue terrestrial timing (RECALL).
evidence.label: FACT (listings) / RECALL (strategy)

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Time transfer lives inside waveforms and crypto (classified, prime-owned); clocks are a mature hardware oligopoly; the integrating customer is diffuse.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Software-only cross-network timing observability (holdover state, drift, source lineage) exposed as ASPN-style time-integrity messages to C2; hardware-agnostic.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Agent that reads timing status from NTP/PTP servers and radios' management interfaces and produces a time-trust map for the network operations cell.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Device management telemetry; access to radio/net management interfaces (often controlled).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Radio and crypto management planes, NTP/PTP, Link 16 net management; certification with USNO.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Only via a prime or DISA/NIWC SBIR; no open solicitation identified in this run.
candidate_gaps.why_now: GPS-denied exercises increasing; but no procurement signal specific to timing assurance software surfaced.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Access to classified waveform/crypto interfaces; product becomes a feature of timing-server vendors.

candidate_gaps.title: GPS-denied visual/terrain navigation software for small UAS and ground vehicles as a standalone PNT product
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Cheap drones and vehicles need absolute positioning without GPS, and DoD has demonstrated 10 m-class terrestrial image navigation, but the capability is being delivered inside autonomy stacks (Skydio, Shield AI, Auterion, Maxar Raptor) rather than as an open, platform-agnostic PNT source that feeds pntOS/ASPN.
